newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Easdaq aims to have 50 listings by end of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Easdaq aims to have 50 listings by end of 1997.

text.p: Europe's new growth stocks market Easdaq, which went live last month, aims to have 50 listings by the end of next year and 500 companies by the year 2001, Easdaq CEO Jacques Putzeys said on Tuesday.
"Today we have three companies. By the end of the week there will will be four and we plan to have 500 in five years' time," he told a presentation in Lisbon.
He said there were 25 to 30 companies from different European countries currently seeking listings.
"The future will be in small, growth companies. Big companies are losing jobs now, while smaller companies are creating them," Putzeys said.
But he admitted that the new market, which specialises in fast-growing companies that carry a higher risk than blue-chips, would have to reassure investors by conducting thorough research.
"We need market makers who've done their homework, who understand the companies and who can inspire investor confidence," he said.
He said the market would be driven by institutional investors.
Already traded on Easdaq are Dr Solomon's Group Plc, a U.K.-based anti-virus software developer, Belgian biotechnology firm Innogenetics and Belgian software company Artwork Systems Group NV.

The initial public offering of the fourth company, French smart card maker ActivCard SA, has been priced at $8 a share, lower than the original $10-$20 price range in view of the poor climate in equity markets over the past few days.
